as_written_in_papers.quote: missense GFAP heterozygous variant NM_002055.5: c.54G>T (p/Gly18Val)
which causes the glycine to valine amino acid substitution at codon 18 (p/Gly18Val) in the GFAP.
Casasnovas et al. identified a heterozygous GFAP c.53G>T (p/Gly18Val) variant in six adults

cases.statement: One carrier in the batch: a Polish boy with onset at 13 years and diagnosis at 15 (heterozygous). The paper's Tables 2 and 3 also list six members of the Casasnovas et al. 2019 family (PMID 31004048, not in the batch) with p/Gly18Val; they are not rows of this candidate.

people.label: patient (Our Patient)
people.key_phenotypes: progressive spastic paraparesis from age 13 with right predominance; brisk reflexes, ankle clonus, bilateral extensor plantars; scoliosis; T2 signal in anterior medulla and cervical cord atrophy on re-evaluated MRI; memory impairment with IQ decline from 98 to 85

quotes.quote: A previously healthy 14½-year-old boy was admitted to the Pediatric Neurology Department with a progressive gait disturbance, beginning at age 13 with insidious lower-limb stiffness and weakness and in-toeing, more pronounced on the right
with bilateral sustained ankle clonus (right > left) and bilateral extensor plantar responses (Babinski positive) (Video S1).
| Scoliosis | Yes | No | Yes | Yes | No | Yes | Yes |
Arrows indicate areas of increased signal in the anterior portions of the medulla oblongata and the anterior horns of the spinal cord.
In our patient, we observed a decrease in IQ from 98 to 85 at the 16-month follow-up.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Isolated progressive spastic paraparesis; the authors note bulbar, autonomic and oculomotor features typical of adult AxD were absent. A hereditary spastic paraplegia NGS panel, MLD and VLCFA tests were negative, and a wide infectious/autoimmune/metabolic work-up was negative. The patient also had craniofacial and somatic dysmorphism, which the paper does not discuss further.

quotes.quote: The patient was referred to the Rehabilitation Department while awaiting results of an NGS panel for hereditary spastic paraplegia, a dried-blood-spot (DBS) assay for metachromatic leukodystrophy, and very-long-chain fatty acids (VLCFA) to exclude adrenoleukodystrophy. All these investigations were negative.
Given an unremarkable family history, the absence of abnormalities on brain and cervical MRI and MR spectroscopy, and the lack of characteristic clinical features of type II AxD
Craniofacial and somatic dysmorphism included triangular facies, a short webbed neck, low posterior hairline, chest wall deformity, and a right supernumerary nipple
Our patient did not exhibit the oculomotor abnormalities reported in all other individuals carrying the same mutation, nor the bladder dysfunction described in two of the six familial cases.

segregation.statement: No relatives of this patient were tested; family history available only on the maternal side and negative. Second-hand: Casasnovas et al. (not in the batch) identified six family members carrying p/Gly18Val.

quotes.quote: Unfortunately, genetic testing of the patient’s family for the presence of the pathogenic variant could not be performed.
Family history was available only on the maternal side and was negative for neurological disease.
The authors of this study identified 6 family members with the same mutation.

de_novo.statement: Parents not tested; de novo status unknown.

quotes.quote: Unfortunately, genetic testing of the patient’s family for the presence of the pathogenic variant could not be performed.

functional.statement: No assay in this paper. Second-hand only: the paper says Casasnovas et al. (not in the batch) concluded from clinical data and functional studies that p/Gly18Val is less deleterious than most AxD variants; assay details are not given.

quotes.quote: They suggested, based on clinical data and functional studies, that this variant is less deleterious than the vast majority of Alexander disease mutations, giving rise to an attenuated clinical phenotype.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: As written in the paper: missense, glycine to valine at codon 18 in the N-terminal head domain. The batch HGVS c.54G>T on NM_002055.5 predicts a synonymous change p.(Gly18=), not a missense (see concerns). The paper states a gain-of-function mechanism for GFAP variants.

quotes.quote: Alexander disease (AxD) is a rare leukodystrophy caused by gain-of-function mutations in the glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) gene
a novel GFAP N-terminal head domain variant (p/Gly18Val)

population_data_in_papers.statement: Described only as 'rare' / 'extremely rare'; no database or frequency given.

quotes.quote: Whole exome sequencing revealed an extremely rare missense GFAP heterozygous variant NM_002055.5: c.54G>T (p/Gly18Val), confirming the diagnosis of AxD.

authors_classification.statement: The authors refer to it as 'the pathogenic variant' and say it confirmed the diagnosis; no formal ACMG classification is given.

quotes.quote: Unfortunately, genetic testing of the patient’s family for the presence of the pathogenic variant could not be performed.
Whole exome sequencing revealed an extremely rare missense GFAP heterozygous variant NM_002055.5: c.54G>T (p/Gly18Val), confirming the diagnosis of AxD.

concerns: Numbering problem: the paper writes c.54G>T throughout (abstract, results, conclusions) but describes it as glycine to valine at codon 18. On NM_002055.5, c.54G>T predicts p.(Gly18=) (batch protein_check: differs). The same paper writes the Casasnovas variant as c.53G>T (p/Gly18Val) and says 'the same variant was detected in the present case'. c.54G>T is therefore probably a nomenclature error for c.53G>T, and the batch VCF (17:44915433:C:A, derived from c.54) may point to the wrong base. The panel should resolve the cDNA position before adjudicating; if the true change is c.53G>T, this candidate may not be a gap variant at all.

Carriers missing from the batch: six Casasnovas et al. family members (I:2, II:2, II:3, II:5, III:4, III:5) are listed in Tables 2 and 3 with the same protein change, without cDNA; they are second-hand from PMID 31004048, which is not in the batch.

Citation inconsistency in the paper: the literature-review paragraph cites Casasnovas et al. as reference [7], but reference [7] is Paprocka et al. (PMID 38540409); elsewhere Casasnovas is reference [17].

The patient has dysmorphic features (triangular facies, short webbed neck, low posterior hairline, chest wall deformity, supernumerary nipple) that the paper does not address; whether exome analysis looked for another cause of these is not stated.
The paper's MRI was first read as normal and re-read at follow-up as showing medullary signal change.
notes_for_panel: Resolve the cDNA position (c.54 vs c.53) first; the paper's own text supports p.Gly18Val and the same variant as Casasnovas et al.
